source.citation: Lonial S, Waller EK, Richardson PG, et al. Risk factors and kinetics of thrombocytopenia associated with bortezomib for relapsed, refractory multiple myeloma. Blood. 2005;106(12):3777-3784.
source.storage: PMC printout kept on the platform owner's computer only; quotes checked against its text layer on 2026-10-14.
source.population: 228 patients with relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma (SUMMIT, CREST), bortezomib 1.3 mg/m2 days 1, 4, 8, 11 of 21-day cycles

grading.system: NCI Common Toxicity Criteria version 2.0 (as used by the source)
grading.grade_1: 75 to below the laboratory lower limit of normal; not drawn because the limit is laboratory-specific
grading.quote: grade 2, 50 × 109/L or greater to less than 75 × 109/L; grade 3, 10 × 109/L or greater to less than 50 × 109/L; grade 4, less than 10 × 109/L
grading.note: Current CTCAE versions place the grade 3/4 boundaries differently; they are not used here, so that the grade lines and the observed incidences share one definition.

eligibility.quote: a platelet count of 50 × 109/L or greater; if they had extensive bone marrow involvement, the threshold was lowered to 30 × 109/L or greater

observed.quote: The incidence of all grades of treatment-emergent thrombocytopenia with bortezomib 1.3 mg/m2 was 42% (96 of 228 patients)
The incidence of grade 3/4 thrombocytopenia was 30% (68 of 228 patients) and it was inversely related to the baseline platelet count
Grade 4 thrombocytopenia (< 10 × 109/L) occurred in 24% of patients with baseline platelet counts less than 70 × 109/L, whereas its incidence was low (≤ 1%) in patients with higher baseline counts
an approximately 60% reduction in platelet counts from start to nadir, regardless of their baseline platelet count
observed.use: Shown as an illustrative line at 40% of the patient's baseline: the average patient's own lowest count, not a prediction for this patient.

limits: Incidences are from adverse-event reporting in one pooled phase 2 population; patients could receive transfusions and dose holds.
The baseline split at 70 x1e9/L is the source's; no finer relationship is extracted (Figure 1 is an image).
